title: AI Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit AI providers, economics, knowledge, assistants, tools, recovery, and verification.
owner: Nodics AI modules and every invoked capability owner
summary: Every AI feature declares authority, configuration, identity, data, model/provider, budgets, tools, approval, lifecycle, observability, failure, and release evidence.

sections.heading: Deployment readiness
items: Begin disabled and enable only approved providers, models, sources, tools, budgets, and audiences with isolated customer-project deployments.
Document business and security owners, classification, regions, retention, escalation, service objectives, cost, qualification, and kill-switch procedure.
Mocked or no-credit tests prove contracts only; production needs authorized live-provider security, usage, cost, timeout, cancellation, outage, and recovery evidence.

sections.heading: Module authority map
items: aiProviders owns normalized provider selection, adapters, models, credentials, limits, usage, and cost; callers never import OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or future vendor SDKs.
aiKnowledge owns governed sources, ingestion, versions, retrieval evidence, and citations while nSearch executes indexes and owning modules expose authorized projections.
aiAssistant owns conversations, turns, SSE events, orchestration, confirmation, cancellation, and recovery; Workflow and target modules retain durable process and business authority.

sections.heading: Provider and cost contract
items: Callers request an approved usage profile and operation; gateway resolves compatible active provider/model, reviewed pricing, secret reference, budgets, rate, circuit, fallback, and kill switches.
Reserve estimated usage atomically, normalize input/output/cache/reasoning tokens, reconcile provider usage, and retain tenant-safe price provenance without storing secrets.
Fallback preserves data classification, region, capability, output contract, budget, and accounting; unknown pricing or exhausted quota never fails open.

sections.heading: Knowledge and assistant lifecycle
items: Ingest through source-owned services, normalize, hash, chunk, embed through aiProviders where configured, index through nSearch, validate, and activate a version with rollback.
Retrieval filters tenant, audience, classification, locale, permission, freshness, and active version before evidence and returns citations or an explicit insufficient-evidence result.
Assistant accepts idempotent turns, leases background work, streams persisted cursor events over authenticated SSE, and handles disconnect, cancellation, provider timeout, and uncertain outcome.

sections.heading: Tools, security, and verification
items: Tool contracts come from current approved backend APIs; read and mutation risks differ, material arguments bind to explicit confirmation, and target modules authorize every call.

Retrieved text and model output are untrusted. Test prompt injection, tool confusion, argument substitution, approval replay, tenant leakage, secrets, excessive agency, provider outage, and cost races.
Qualify groundedness, refusal, citations, latency, streaming, reconnect, cancellation, leases, workflow handoff, idempotency, retention, redaction, live providers, load, recovery, and regression.

sections.heading: Checklist
items: Usage profile, provider capabilities, model, reviewed pricing, secret reference, timeout, cancellation, fallback, rate, circuit, and kill switch.
Tenant, enterprise, project, user, conversation, operation budgets, reservation, ledger, reconciliation, and retention.
Corpus/source ownership, schema/service read contract, chunking, embedding, search mode, version, freshness, permission, evidence, and citation.
Assistant definition, approved prompt, context/redaction, conversation ownership, SSE events, leases, cancellation, recovery, tools, confirmation, and Workflow handoff.
No direct database/search/provider/tool authority bypass.
Positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, concurrency, prompt-injection, authorization, cost, load, outage, recovery, live-provider, security, and regression tests.
